content:
# Issues and labels

All paths begin `/api/v1`. Session mutations send `X-Crew-Request: 1`; API tokens require the named scope in addition to the actor's project access. Members write issues; guests read only granted projects. Lists accept `limit` (1–200, default 50), opaque `cursor`, and return `{items,nextCursor}`. Organization issue lists apply project access before pagination.

`GET/POST /projects/:projectId/issues` lists or creates issues. `GET /orgs/:orgId/issues` lists accessible organization issues. Filters are `statusId`, `assigneeId`, `labelId`, `priority`, `q` (case insensitive key/title/description substring). `GET/PATCH/DELETE /issues/:issueId` reads, updates or deletes an issue. Read needs `project:read`; mutation needs `issue:write`. Archived projects remain readable and reject mutations with 409.

Create takes `{title,description,statusId,priority,assigneeId,estimate,dueDate,parentId,labelIds}`. Title is 1–300 characters. Description preserves Markdown whitespace and is at most 100000 characters. Omitted status uses the first ordered workflow state. Priority is 0 none, 1 urgent, 2 high, 3 normal, 4 low. Estimate is nullable, finite, between 0 and 1000000; fractions and zero are valid. Due date is nullable YYYY-MM-DD and must be a real calendar date. Assignee needs project access. Parent must be in the same project and cannot create a cycle. Every label must belong to the project. PATCH retains omitted fields and accepts null for assignee, estimate, due date and parent; `labelIds:[]` clears labels. Unknown fields and invalid inputs return 422 with field details.

Issue keys use the project key and sequential number. Numbers allocate transactionally; failed requests do not consume them and deletion does not reuse them. Public issues include all fields plus `id,orgId,projectId,projectKey,number,key,statusName,statusCategory,assignee,creator,createdBy,rank,labels,createdAt,updatedAt`. No password or token fields are exposed.

`GET/POST /projects/:projectId/labels` lists or creates `{name,color}`. Names are unique within a project ignoring case; colors use six hexadecimal digits such as `#5965d8`. `PATCH/DELETE /labels/:labelId` updates or removes a label. Removing one also removes assignments. Label changes emit updated full issue snapshots for affected issues so indexes stay current.

The web offers project issue filters with cursor loading, complete create/edit forms, parent and label controls, issue detail and child links, and a label manager. Required and invalid fields have accessible errors. Destructive operations ask for confirmation.

CLI: `crew issue list PROJECT [--status ID --assignee ID --label ID --priority N --query TEXT --limit N --cursor CURSOR]`, `create PROJECT --title TEXT`, `show ISSUE`, `edit ISSUE`, `delete ISSUE --yes`. Create/edit support `--description`, `--description-file`, `--status`, `--priority`, `--assignee`, `--estimate`, `--due`, `--parent`, `--labels ID,ID`. Use `none` to clear nullable fields or labels. Label actions are `labels PROJECT`, `label-create PROJECT --name TEXT [--color HEX]`, `label-edit LABEL`, `label-delete LABEL --yes`. All commands support global `--json`, `--url`, `--token`, `--config`.

## Integration schema and events

Migrations 200–249 belong to W1. `issues(id,project_id,number,title,description,status_id,priority,assignee_id,estimate,due_date,parent_id,created_by,rank,created_at,updated_at)` stores issue content. `labels(id,project_id,name,color,created_at,updated_at)` and `issue_labels(issue_id,label_id)` store project label assignments. Parent deletion clears children; issue deletion cascades assignments. Project deletion cascades issues and labels.

`modules/work/issues.js` exports the canonical `getIssue(ctx,id)` hydrated reader, `publicIssue(row)`, `listIssues(ctx,projectId,query)`, `createIssue`, `updateIssue`, `deleteIssue`, `emitIssue`, `validateIssueReferences` and `replaceIssueLabels`. Consumers should reuse `getIssue` rather than create another encoder. `publicIssue` takes the joined issueSelect row; use getIssue for labels.

Issue events use entityType `issue`, action `created`, `updated`, `deleted`, full before/after snapshots, actorId, orgId, projectId, entityId and UTC time. Label events use entityType `label` and the same actions. Emit occurs after the synchronous transaction has committed. Full issue after data contains descriptions, assignee identity, creator identity and label objects for search and notification consumers.

## Comments, Markdown and mentions

GET/POST /issues/:issueId/comments lists or creates {body}. PATCH/DELETE /comments/:commentId edits or removes a comment. Reads need project:read; writes need comment:write. An author can edit/remove their own comments; an organization owner/admin may manage other comments. Granted guests can comment. Archived projects reject discussion writes. Lists are chronological and cursor paginated. Comments return author identity, original body, safe html, mentionedUserIds and timestamps.

Markdown supports headings, paragraphs, line breaks, ordered/unordered/task lists, block quotes, horizontal rules, inline/fenced code, emphasis, bold, strikeout and links. All raw HTML and attribute delimiters are escaped. Only http, https and mailto links are active. Code never produces mentions. Mention syntax is @handle, @email, @{userId}, or @[Display name](user:userId). Name/email/id matching is case insensitive and resolves only organization members with access to this project. The web mention picker inserts explicit IDs to avoid name ambiguity. Unknown mentions remain text. No HTML is trusted from the user.

Comment events use entityType comment and created/updated/deleted actions. After contains the full comment, a hydrated issue snapshot, mentionedUserIds and userIds; event also has issueId and mentionedUserIds. Consumers can subscribe creator, assignee and mentioned users through these IDs. Table comments(id,issue_id,author_id,body,created_at,updated_at) cascades on issue deletion. Reuse getComment(ctx,id), listComments(ctx,issueId), publicComment(ctx,row).

## Issue relations

GET/POST /issues/:issueId/relations lists or creates {targetIssueId,kind}. DELETE /relations/:relationId removes a relation. Reads need project:read and hide inaccessible opposite endpoints before pagination. Writes need issue:write on both projects and both must be in the same organization and unarchived. Self relations are invalid. blocks and duplicates are directed source to target; their inverse views read blocked by and duplicated by. An issue can duplicate only one original. Directed cycles are rejected. relates is symmetric, stored in canonical ID order; reversed duplicates return 409. Different relation kinds may coexist.

Relations return sourceIssueId,targetIssueId,kind,direction,caption,relatedIssue,createdBy,createdAt. Table issue_relations(id,source_issue_id,target_issue_id,kind,created_by,created_at) cascades when either issue is deleted. Events use entityType relation and created/deleted actions with complete before/after relation, issueId, actor/org/project identity and UTC time.

CLI discussion actions: comments ISSUE, comment ISSUE --body TEXT (or --body-file FILE), comment-edit COMMENT --body TEXT, comment-delete COMMENT --yes, relations ISSUE, relate ISSUE --target ISSUE --kind blocks|duplicates|relates, unrelate RELATION --yes. The issue page offers Markdown previews, mention picker, comment editing/removal and relation controls with inverse labels.
